value.message:
This plugin allows you to enforce protection rules around whether records can be updated, deleted, or inserted for the following system log tables: 

  • syslog
  • syslog_app_scope
  • syslog_transaction
  • sys_outbound_http_log
  • sysevent
  • sys_audit
  • sys_push_notification 

For each system log table you can specify one of 4 protection levels:

  1. Block changes (Only block the attempt)
  2. Log changes (Only log the attempt)
  3. Block and log changes (Block and log the attempt)
  4. Allow changes (Don’t block and don’t log the attempt)

According to the policies, any record-modifying operations from the user interface or via script will be intercepted by the platform and be blocked and/or logged.

The platform will use the Log Protection levels assigned to update, delete, and insert operations of system log tables to block and/or log any attempted operation. Any operations from the user interface or via script will be intercepted by the platform and be blocked and/or logged. 

An admin with the security_admin role elevation can override the default log protection levels for each of the tables to adjust the behavior based on customizations made to your platform. However, there are some tables whose protection levels cannot be changed: syslog and syslog_app_scope have fixed values for update and delete protections, and protected_table_configuration has fixed protection values for all three operations. Additionally, insert protections for sysevent cannot be set to block changes.

Attempts to modify the system log tables are logged to the protected_table_log table.  Entries written to this table are driven by the configuration.  If a protection level of “Log” is not specified for a table, then any attempt to modify the given table will not be logged to protected_table_log.

Also, any configuration changes made for this plugin will also be logged to protected_table_log.
How can I see apps or users that tried to modify a log?

For each of the protected log tables, you can assign a combination of “Block”, “Log”, or “Do nothing” for update and delete operations.

The valid options are:

  • Block and log the attempt
  • Only block the attempt
  • Only log the attempt
  • Don’t block and don’t log the attempt

When blocking is configured for an update/delete/insert operation, all UI actions allowing that operation will be removed, and any attempts to perform the operation on the table via script will not succeed.

When logging is configured, any attempt via UI action or script to update/delete/insert records in the table will not be restricted, however, the change will be logged in protected_table_log.

When “Don’t block and don’t log the attempt” is configured, the plugin will not track or restrict modifications to the data in that table.
